no_rerun.reason: The correction changes the DIRECTION of a bound label that is only ever consumed by equality tests against 'exact'. It cannot move any measured node count, wall clock, value, mate or plan. Re-running the sweep would produce evidence about a different question.

defect.code_as_written: const strictBound = PVS_STRICT_BOUNDS && degenerateWindow; const boundType = strictBound ? (maximizing ? 'lower' : 'upper') : ...
defect.claimed_justification_in_code_comment: a node that entered with a degenerate window is an unresolved bound in BOTH directions (MAX can only prove `<= X`, MIN can only prove `>= X`), whatever the cutoff flag says
defect.what_is_wrong: The comment states the correct fact (MAX proves <= X, MIN proves >= X) and then emits the OPPOSITE labels. A MAX result of `value <= X` is an UPPER bound; arm D labels it 'lower'. A MIN result of `value >= X` is a LOWER bound; arm D labels it 'upper'. Both directions are inverted.

correct_mapping.degenerate_window_max_cut_off: lower  (proved: true value >= X == beta) — unchanged, this one was already right
correct_mapping.degenerate_window_min_cut_off: upper  (proved: true value <= X == alpha) — unchanged, this one was already right

defect.why_the_case_is_reachable_only_because_a: Arm D also relaxed the degenerate-window cutoff test from `>= 0` to `> 0` (lines 1569/1571), which is what allows a degenerate node to finish WITHOUT cutting off. Under the production `>=` rule a (X,X) node cuts off on its first candidate, so the mislabelled branch would have been dead code. The label and the relaxation were introduced together.

blast_radius_audit.question: does the inverted direction change any PPC-SEARCH-01 number?
blast_radius_audit.finding: Every consumer tests equality against 'exact'. 'lower' and 'upper' are indistinguishable to all of them, so swapping the two labels is INERT for storage, certification, tie-break eligibility and plan extraction.
unaffected_conclusions: G1T10 arm D node count 12,225 -> 365,612 (668x production) — driven by `bound !== 'exact'` barring the EXACT-only TT, not by which non-exact label was used
NO_GO_PVS verdict and all three supporting reasons
the bound-contract gap in production (expectiminimax.ts:1422 states the cutoff axis, not the window axis) — that is a DIFFERENT, still-open finding
blast_radius_audit.newly_weakened_claim: PPC-SEARCH-01 §7.4 called arm D 'the bound fix'. Correct description: 'a conservative non-exact labelling, with the two labels swapped'. It remains sufficient to demonstrate that refusing EXACT writes destroys the cache economics (that is what the 668x measures), but it is NOT a correct implementation of window-axis honesty, so it must not be cited as one.

implication_for_future_rounds: Any future narrow-window work must emit MAX-no-cutoff -> 'upper', MIN-no-cutoff -> 'lower', and must add a FOURTH state to InternalSearchResult.bound (e.g. 'narrowed-unresolved') if it ever wants to distinguish 'proved exact' from 'window-limited', because 'lower'/'upper' in this codebase are ALSO produced by real alpha-beta cutoffs and the two meanings are not separable today.
The production defect at expectiminimax.ts:1422 (bound tracks the cutoff axis only) is still open and still blocks any window-narrowing search. The PVS line stays closed.
